trex.label: the two-legged hunters
trex.desc: They walk on two legs and hunt
trex.sci_sens: In Greek, thero means wild beast, and pod means foot.
trex.explic: Theropods! In Greek, thero means wild beast, and pod means foot. They got that name because they walked on two big back legs, just like birds do today — not on four! Almost all of them ate meat. The famous ones: T. rex, Spinosaurus, Giganotosaurus.

cou_long.label: the long-necked giants
cou_long.desc: A huge neck for reaching the treetops
cou_long.sci_sens: In Greek, sauro means lizard, and pod means foot.
cou_long.explic: Sauropods! In Greek, sauro means lizard, and pod means foot. These are the biggest animals that ever walked on Earth! Four legs like tree trunks, and a huge neck for reaching leaves way up high. They only ate plants. The stars: Diplodocus, Brachiosaurus, Brontosaurus.

arme.label: the spiky armor-backs
arme.desc: Plates, spikes, and a club tail
arme.sci_sens: In Greek, thyreo means shield, and phor means to carry.
arme.explic: Thyreophorans! In Greek, thyreo means shield, and phor means to carry: the shield-carriers. Their backs were covered in plates, spikes, and bony armor to protect them from hunters. They munched on plants. The famous ones: Stegosaurus, with plates on its back, and Ankylosaurus, with a big bony club at the end of its tail.

cornu.label: the horned frill-faces
cornu.desc: Horns and a big bony frill
cornu.sci_sens: In Greek, cerat means horn, and ops means face.
cornu.explic: Ceratopsians! In Greek, cerat means horn, and ops means face: the horned faces. They had horns on their heads and a big bony frill behind the skull, like a shield around the neck. They ate plants. The superstar: Triceratops, and its cousin Torosaurus.

bec.label: the duck-bills
bec.desc: A flat beak and huge herds
bec.sci_sens: In Greek, ornitho means bird, and pod means foot.
bec.explic: Ornithopods! In Greek, ornitho means bird, and pod means foot: bird feet. Their legs looked like a bird's. They had a wide, flat beak like a duck for munching plants, and lived in huge herds. All of them ate plants. The famous ones: Parasaurolophus and Iguanodon.

raptor.label: the claw hunters
raptor.sci_sens: In Greek, dromaeo means one who runs, and saur means lizard.
raptor.explic: Dromaeosaurs! In Greek, dromaeo means one who runs fast, and saur means lizard: the running lizards. They're cousins of the theropods, but smaller, faster, and smarter, with one big curved claw shaped like a sickle on each foot for grabbing prey. They ate meat. The stars: Velociraptor and the bigger Deinonychus.

pterosaures.label: the flying reptiles
pterosaures.sci_sens: In Greek, ptero means wing, and saur means lizard.
pterosaures.explic: Pterosaurs! In Greek, ptero means wing, and saur means lizard: the winged lizards. Careful, these are not dinosaurs — they're their cousins! They glided on huge wings made of skin, like a living kite. The famous ones: Pteranodon, and the giant Quetzalcoatlus, as big as a small plane!

enaliosaures.label: the giant sea reptiles
enaliosaures.desc: Not dinosaurs — giant reptiles that swam!
enaliosaures.sci_sens: In Greek, enalio means of the sea, and saur means lizard.
enaliosaures.explic: Enaliosaurs! In Greek, enalio means of the sea, and saur means lizard: the sea lizards. Careful, these are NOT dinosaurs! They're giant reptiles that lived at the same time, but in the OCEAN. Some had a very long neck, others a huge hunting mouth, and one of them was a giant turtle! The stars: long-necked Elasmosaurus, hunter Liopleurodon, giant turtle Archelon, and the ichthyosaurs Shonisaurus and Shastasaurus.

volant.label: the cousin from before the dinos
volant.desc: It lived long before the dinosaurs!
volant.sci_sens: Surprise: they lived BEFORE the dinosaurs!
volant.explic: Careful, these are NOT dinosaurs! They lived a very, very long time BEFORE them. And here's the wild part: they're distant cousins of furry animals — so a little bit of you! There's Dimetrodon and Edaphosaurus, who carried a big sail on their backs; Gorgonops, a hunter with saber teeth; little Lystrosaurus, who survived the biggest disaster the Earth ever saw; and Moschops, with a skull as thick as a helmet.

mammiferes.label: the furry beasts after the dinos
mammiferes.desc: After the dinos: the furry giants
mammiferes.sci_sens: A mammal is a furry animal whose mom makes milk for her babies — just like you!
mammiferes.explic: Mammals! These are furry animals, whose mom feeds her babies milk — like a cat, a dog, or you! When the giant meteorite made the dinosaurs disappear, mammals were the ones who took over the whole planet. Some of them grew enormous! The stars: the fuzzy Woolly Mammoth, Smilodon with its giant teeth, and Paraceratherium, the biggest furry animal that ever walked the Earth.

oiseaux.label: the giant birds that couldn't fly
oiseaux.desc: Giant hunting birds that couldn't fly
oiseaux.sci_sens: Birds are the living cousins of dinosaurs — the only ones still around today!
oiseaux.explic: Birds! Want to know a secret? Birds are the little cousins of dinosaurs — they're the only dinosaur family still alive today! But after the meteorite, some birds grew GIANT, too heavy to fly. They ran on two big legs to hunt, with a huge beak. The star: Titanis, the terror bird!

tyrannosaurus.name: T. rex
tyrannosaurus.comp_taille: as long as a school bus!
tyrannosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a double-decker bus!
tyrannosaurus.nom_etym: "Tyrannosaurus Rex" splits into three parts! Tyranno, in Greek, is a ruler who answers to no one — nobody can tell him no. Saurus, or "saur," is Greek for lizard. And Rex, in Latin, means king. All together: the tyrant lizard king!
tyrannosaurus.superpower: The strongest bite of any dinosaur that walked on land!
tyrannosaurus.chasseurs: Nobody dared attack it... it was the king!
tyrannosaurus.amis: Mostly a loner, but maybe family groups sometimes
tyrannosaurus.fait: Its teeth were 8 inches long — longer than your hand! And it had 60 of them!
tyrannosaurus.desc: T. rex is the king of the dinosaurs. It had a huge head, giant teeth, and tiny little arms. But watch out — its back legs could run really fast!

spinosaurus.name: Spinosaurus
spinosaurus.comp_taille: as long as a school bus!
spinosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a double-decker bus!
spinosaurus.comp_poids: as heavy as an elephant and a rhino put together!
spinosaurus.nom_etym: "Spinosaurus" is half Latin, half Greek! Spino, in Latin, means spine — like the tall spikes of the sail on its back. And saurus (or "saur"), in Greek, means lizard. All together: the spined lizard!
spinosaurus.superpower: Swam like a giant crocodile! It loved the water.
spinosaurus.fait: The sail on its back could stand almost 7 feet tall — as tall as a front door!
spinosaurus.desc: Spinosaurus was even bigger than T. rex! It lived near rivers and caught huge fish. It had a big red sail on its back.

giganotosaurus.name: Giganotosaurus
giganotosaurus.comp_taille: as long as a school bus!
giganotosaurus.comp_hauteur: like two Dads standing on each other's shoulders!
giganotosaurus.comp_poids: as heavy as an elephant and a rhino put together!
giganotosaurus.nom_etym: "Giganotosaurus," three Greek pieces! Giga means giant — like "gigantic"! Noto means from the south (it lived way down south, in Argentina). And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the giant lizard from the south!
giganotosaurus.superpower: Hunted in packs to take down ENORMOUS sauropods!
giganotosaurus.proies: Andesaurus, a huge long-necked dinosaur that lived in the same area
giganotosaurus.amis: May have hunted in packs, like lions
giganotosaurus.fait: It's the biggest carnivore in South America! Even bigger than T. rex!
giganotosaurus.desc: Giganotosaurus lived in South America. It was ENORMOUS and may have hunted in packs to catch dinosaurs even bigger than itself!

carcharodontosaurus.name: Carcharodontosaurus
carcharodontosaurus.comp_taille: as long as a school bus!
carcharodontosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as two Dads standing on each other's shoulders!
carcharodontosaurus.comp_poids: as heavy as an elephant and a rhino put together!
carcharodontosaurus.nom_etym: "Carcharodontosaurus," three Greek pieces! Charcharo means jagged and sharp — it's where the word "shark" comes from! Odonto means tooth. And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the shark-toothed lizard!
carcharodontosaurus.superpower: Teeth shaped like shark teeth — cutting like a knife!
carcharodontosaurus.fait: Its name means "shark-toothed lizard"! Its teeth were serrated like a saw!
carcharodontosaurus.desc: Carcharodontosaurus lived in Africa at the same time as Spinosaurus. It had teeth shaped like shark teeth for slicing through its food.

allosaurus.name: Allosaurus
allosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a double-decker bus!
allosaurus.nom_etym: "Allosaurus," two Greek pieces! Allo means other, different — its bones didn't look like any other. And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the different lizard!
allosaurus.superpower: Opened its jaw SUPER wide like an axe to strike!
allosaurus.chasseurs: Nothing in its time dared face it alone
allosaurus.fait: The T. rex of the Jurassic! Scientists found hundreds of its bones in a single spot!
allosaurus.desc: Allosaurus was the top hunter of the Jurassic. It opened its jaw super wide to strike its prey like a swing of an axe!

tarbosaurus.name: Tarbosaurus
tarbosaurus.comp_taille: as long as a school bus!
tarbosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a double-decker bus!
tarbosaurus.nom_etym: "Tarbosaurus," two Greek pieces! Tarbo means fear, dread — the one who makes everyone tremble. And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the alarming lizard!
tarbosaurus.superpower: The T. rex of Asia — a direct cousin!
tarbosaurus.fait: It's T. rex's Asian cousin! It lived in the Gobi Desert in Mongolia.
tarbosaurus.desc: Tarbosaurus was Asia's T. rex! It lived in the deserts of Mongolia and looked a lot like its American cousin.

albertosaurus.name: Albertosaurus
albertosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a basketball hoop!
albertosaurus.nom_etym: "Albertosaurus" is named after a place! Alberta is a big region in Canada where its bones were found. And saurus (or saur), in Greek, lizard. All together: the Alberta lizard!
albertosaurus.superpower: May have hunted in packs! The wolf of the T. rex family!
albertosaurus.amis: May have lived in groups — 26 skeletons were found together!
albertosaurus.fait: 26 Albertosaurs were found together in Canada! They may have hunted in packs like wolves!
albertosaurus.desc: Albertosaurus was smaller than T. rex but very clever. It may have hunted in packs, like wolves do today!

ceratosaurus.name: Ceratosaurus
ceratosaurus.region: North America (and maybe Europe, in Portugal)
ceratosaurus.comp_taille: as long as a road is wide — it takes up the whole street!
ceratosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a front door!
ceratosaurus.comp_poids: as heavy as a small car!
ceratosaurus.nom_etym: "Ceratosaurus," two Greek pieces! Cerato means horn — it had one on its nose! And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the horned lizard!
ceratosaurus.superpower: It had ONE horn on its nose — unique among the big carnivores!
ceratosaurus.fait: It had small horns on its head and one big horn on its nose — the only big carnivore with a horn!
ceratosaurus.desc: Ceratosaurus had something special: a horn on its nose! It lived in the Jurassic and hunted small animals and fish.

dilophosaurus.name: Dilophosaurus
dilophosaurus.comp_taille: like two cars, one behind the other!
dilophosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a soccer goal!
dilophosaurus.nom_etym: "Dilophosaurus," three Greek pieces! Di means two. Lopho means crest. And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the two-crested lizard!
dilophosaurus.superpower: 2 colorful crests on its head like a party hat!
dilophosaurus.fait: It had 2 parallel crests on its head — they were probably very colorful, to attract friends!
dilophosaurus.desc: Dilophosaurus had two pretty colorful crests on its head. It's one of the first big carnivorous dinosaurs!

carnotaurus.name: Carnotaurus
carnotaurus.comp_taille: like two cars, one behind the other!
carnotaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a soccer goal!
carnotaurus.comp_poids: as heavy as a small car and a cow put together!
carnotaurus.nom_etym: "Carnotaurus," two Latin pieces! Carno, in Latin, means meat, flesh. And taurus means bull — it had two horns, just like a bull! All together: the meat-eating bull!
carnotaurus.superpower: The FASTEST hunter among the big carnivores — up to 32 miles an hour, as fast as a car in the city!
carnotaurus.fait: It had REAL HORNS above its eyes — like a bull! And it was super fast!
carnotaurus.desc: Carnotaurus had horns like a bull and could run super fast! It's one of the fastest dinosaurs of its whole era.

cryolophosaurus.name: Cryolophosaurus
cryolophosaurus.comp_taille: as long as a road is wide — it takes up the whole street!
cryolophosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a soccer goal!
cryolophosaurus.nom_etym: "Cryolophosaurus," three Greek pieces! Cryo means ice, cold (like when you're freezing!) — it lived in Antarctica. Lopho means crest. And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the ice-crested lizard!
cryolophosaurus.superpower: Lived in Antarctica! The snow dino!
cryolophosaurus.fait: Discovered in Antarctica! It lived there back when it was still warm. And it had a funny fan-shaped crest standing up on its head, like a little wave!
cryolophosaurus.desc: Cryolophosaurus lived in Antarctica back when it was still a little warm there! It had a silly crest running across its head, standing up like a wave — that's what makes it easy to spot!

brachiosaurus.name: Brachiosaurus
brachiosaurus.comp_taille: as long as two school buses!
brachiosaurus.nom_etym: "Brachiosaurus," two Greek pieces! Brachio means arm — its front legs were long like giant arms. And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the arm lizard!
brachiosaurus.superpower: Ate leaves way up in the treetops that nobody else could reach!
brachiosaurus.chasseurs: Only the very biggest carnivores dared attack the young ones
brachiosaurus.fait: Its head reached 43 feet high — as tall as two giraffes stacked up! To digest its food, it swallowed stones to grind it up in its stomach.
brachiosaurus.desc: Brachiosaurus was huge! It ate leaves way up in the treetops. It had a very long neck and big front legs. A gentle giant!
brachiosaurus.queue_note: For this one, it's not the tail that makes the length: it's the huge NECK stretched up toward the sky!

diplodocus.name: Diplodocus
diplodocus.comp_taille: like two buses, one behind the other!
diplodocus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a double-decker bus!
diplodocus.nom_etym: "Diplodocus," two Greek pieces! Diplo means double. And docus means a beam, a big bar — because the bones in its tail had a strange double-beam shape. All together: the double beam!
diplodocus.superpower: Its tail cracked like a whip — CRACK! — to scare off hunters!
diplodocus.chasseurs: Allosaurus, Ceratosaurus for the young ones
diplodocus.fait: Its tail cracked like a whip so fast that scientists think it could have sounded as loud as thunder!
diplodocus.desc: Diplodocus was one of the longest dinosaurs. It had a very long neck AND a very long tail. That tail made a huge whip-crack sound to scare off hunters!
diplodocus.queue_note: Out of its 89 feet, the whip-tail makes up almost half — about 43 feet all by itself!

apatosaurus.name: Apatosaurus (Brontosaurus)
apatosaurus.comp_taille: as long as two school buses!
apatosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a double-decker bus!
apatosaurus.nom_etym: "Apatosaurus," two Greek pieces! Apato means trickery, illusion — its bones fooled scientists for a long time! And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the deceptive lizard!
apatosaurus.superpower: A 20-foot neck for reaching leaves way up high!
apatosaurus.fait: For a long time, people called it "Brontosaurus" — but its real name is Apatosaurus! It ate 550 pounds of plants EVERY DAY!
apatosaurus.desc: Apatosaurus is the gentle giant many people call Brontosaurus. It ate as many plants in one day as you eat in a whole year!
apatosaurus.queue_note: A big part of its length is its very long tail, held out flat and level.

camarasaurus.name: Camarasaurus
camarasaurus.comp_taille: as long as a school bus!
camarasaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a street lamp!
camarasaurus.nom_etym: "Camarasaurus," two Greek pieces! Camara means a chamber, a little room — its bones had hollow spaces like little rooms inside. And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the chambered lizard!
camarasaurus.superpower: Thick teeth for chewing through the toughest branches!
camarasaurus.fait: The most common sauropod in North America! It had big window-like openings in its skull to make its head lighter.
camarasaurus.desc: Camarasaurus was a giant dinosaur with a big head and strong teeth. It lived in herds and took good care of its babies.

amargasaurus.name: Amargasaurus
amargasaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a soccer goal!
amargasaurus.nom_etym: "Amargasaurus" is named after a place! Amarga comes from "La Amarga," the spot in Argentina where it was found — and in Spanish, amarga means "bitter"! And saurus (or saur), in Greek, lizard. All together: the lizard from La Amarga!
amargasaurus.superpower: 2 rows of spikes down its neck! To defend itself, or to look good for friends!
amargasaurus.fait: It had 2 rows of HUGE spikes down its neck and back! Like a living hedge of spikes!
amargasaurus.desc: Amargasaurus had 2 rows of big spikes down its neck and back. It might have used them to defend itself, or to show off to its friends!

plateosaurus.name: Plateosaurus
plateosaurus.comp_taille: like two cars, one behind the other!
plateosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a basketball hoop!
plateosaurus.nom_etym: "Plateosaurus," two Greek pieces! Plateo means wide, flat — like a platter! And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the flat lizard!
plateosaurus.superpower: One of the FIRST big plant-eating dinosaurs — a pioneer!
plateosaurus.chasseurs: The first big carnivores of the Triassic
plateosaurus.fait: One of the first big dinos! It walked on 4 legs but could rear up on 2 to reach the tallest branches.
plateosaurus.desc: Plateosaurus was one of the very first big dinosaurs. It lived in the Triassic, long before T. rex. It could stand up on its back legs to reach higher food!

ankylosaurus.name: Ankylosaurus
ankylosaurus.comp_taille: like two cars, one behind the other!
ankylosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as Dad standing up!
ankylosaurus.nom_etym: "Ankylosaurus," two Greek pieces! Ankylo means fused, stiff, rigid — its whole back was fused together like tough armor. And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the stiff, armored lizard!
ankylosaurus.superpower: Its back was an armor of bony plates, plus a club tail for smashing a T. rex's bones!
ankylosaurus.chasseurs: T. rex might try! But it was very risky: its only weak spots (belly, eyes, legs) were well hidden, and one swing of that club tail could break a carnivore's leg. Better not to bother it!
ankylosaurus.fait: On top it was a real fortress — but its belly had no armor! Luckily it stayed low to the ground, almost hugging it, so it was very hard to flip over.
ankylosaurus.desc: Ankylosaurus was the dinosaur world's tank! Its back was covered in armor as hard as rock, and its tail ended in a big bony club. Even a big carnivore had to be careful: one swing of that club could break its leg!

euoplocephalus.name: Euoplocephalus
euoplocephalus.comp_taille: as long as a road is wide — it takes up the whole street!
euoplocephalus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a car — you'd have to look up!
euoplocephalus.nom_etym: "Euoplocephalus," three Greek pieces! Eu means well. Oplo means a weapon, an armor (like the Greek soldiers called "hoplites"!). And cephalo means head. All together: the well-armored head!
euoplocephalus.superpower: Even its eyelids were armored! Nothing could hurt it!
euoplocephalus.fait: Even ITS EYES had bony armor! The best-protected dino in all of history!
euoplocephalus.desc: Euoplocephalus was even more armored than Ankylosaurus. Even its eyelids were made of bone! It also had a super powerful club tail.

edmontonia.name: Edmontonia
edmontonia.comp_taille: as long as a road is wide — it takes up the whole street!
edmontonia.nom_etym: "Edmontonia" doesn't come from Greek — it's named after a place! It was found near the city of Edmonton, in Canada. So they called it "the one from Edmonton." And rugosidens, in Latin, means rough tooth — a bit bumpy, not smooth.
edmontonia.superpower: Big pointed spikes on its shoulders for defense — no need to run away!
edmontonia.chasseurs: Gorgosaurus and Daspletosaurus, two cousins of T. rex, gave it a try. But with those shoulder spikes, attacking from the side was very dangerous.
edmontonia.fait: Edmontonia had big pointed spikes on its shoulders, but NO club at the end of its tail like Ankylosaurus! To defend itself, it lowered its head and pointed its spikes forward: hard to grab without getting poked.
edmontonia.desc: Edmontonia was a plant-eater covered in armor: bony plates on its back and big spikes on its shoulders. Low to the ground and fully armored, it munched plants peacefully. Unlike Ankylosaurus, it had no club tail: its spikes were defense enough.

minmi.name: Minmi
minmi.comp_taille: like three 4-year-olds lying end to end!
minmi.nom_etym: "Minmi" isn't Greek or Latin like the others! It's named after a place: Minmi Crossing, in Australia, where its bones were found. And "paravertebra" is Latin: para, next to, and vertebra, the backbone — it had strange little bones running along its back. All together: the dino from Minmi Crossing, with strange little bones next to its back! For a long time, it held the record for the shortest dinosaur name in the world!
minmi.superpower: Longer legs than its armored cousins — handy for dashing to safety if a hunter came close!
minmi.chasseurs: Big Australian hunters tried to flip it onto its back, where it had no armor. With its speedy legs, it often got away first.
minmi.fait: Scientists found its very last meal fossilized in its belly: seeds, bits of fruit, and ferns! It's very rare to know EXACTLY what a dinosaur ate before it died.
minmi.desc: Minmi was a small armored dino from Australia. It had armor on its back AND under its belly, which is rare. And for an armored dino, it had long legs: it could dash off to safety.

scutellosaurus.name: Scutellosaurus
scutellosaurus.comp_taille: like a big dog — a Labrador!
scutellosaurus.comp_hauteur: it would come up to your knees!
scutellosaurus.comp_poids: as heavy as a big cat!
scutellosaurus.nom_etym: "Scutellosaurus," two pieces! Scutellum, in Latin, is a little shield. And saurus (or saur), in Greek, lizard. All together: the little-shield lizard — because of the hundreds of tiny bony plates on its back!
scutellosaurus.superpower: The ONLY armored dino that ran on two legs! All its armored cousins that came after, like Ankylosaurus, walked on four legs.
scutellosaurus.chasseurs: Dilophosaurus, a crested hunter, lived in the same area
scutellosaurus.fait: It had over 300 tiny bony plates on its back and tail — but no big armor or club tail like its later cousins. It was the very first version, in a light, early style!
scutellosaurus.desc: Scutellosaurus was tiny: barely longer than a bike, and as light as a big cat. Hundreds of tiny bony plates covered its back like a mosaic. Its long tail worked like a balance pole so it could run on its two back legs.

scelidosaurus.name: Scelidosaurus
scelidosaurus.nom_etym: "Scelidosaurus," two pieces! Saurus (or saur), in Greek, is lizard. And "scelido" — the scientist who named it meant to say "strong legs," because it had really powerful thighs... but he picked the wrong Greek word: the one he actually wrote means "rib of beef"! All together: the strong-legged lizard — with a funny mistake baked right in!
scelidosaurus.superpower: Hundreds of tiny bony studs in its skin, lined up in rows from neck to tail tip — and even two little horns behind its head!
scelidosaurus.chasseurs: Small two-legged hunters were already prowling the area
scelidosaurus.amis: A mystery! Nobody knows yet if it lived alone or in groups
scelidosaurus.fait: Scelidosaurus is one of the very first dinosaurs ever found almost complete! An English worker named James Harrison discovered its bones in a cliff nearly 170 years ago — and its skeleton is still on display today in London's great museum.
scelidosaurus.desc: Scelidosaurus was an armored plant-eater: the great-great-grandfather of the ankylosaurs and stegosaurs, long before them. Its back had hundreds of tiny bony plates lined up in rows, like buttons. It grazed on low plants near the sea, in England.

stegosaurus.name: Stegosaurus
stegosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a basketball hoop!
stegosaurus.nom_etym: "Stegosaurus," two Greek pieces! Stego means roof. And saurus (or saur), lizard. At first, the scientist thought its big plates lay flat on its back, like roof tiles — that's where the name comes from! Later, it turned out they stood straight up instead. All together: the roofed lizard!
stegosaurus.superpower: The big plates on its back worked like a radiator to control its body temperature!
stegosaurus.chasseurs: Allosaurus — but watch out for the tail!
stegosaurus.fait: Its brain was the size of a walnut! But its tail with 4 spikes could stab an Allosaurus!
stegosaurus.desc: Stegosaurus had big colorful plates on its back and 4 long spikes at the end of its tail. Its plates may have worked like a radiator to help it warm up or cool down!

kentrosaurus.name: Kentrosaurus
kentrosaurus.comp_taille: as long as a big SUV!
kentrosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as Dad standing up!
kentrosaurus.comp_poids: as heavy as a small car!
kentrosaurus.nom_etym: "Kentrosaurus," two Greek pieces! Kentro means a sharp point, a spike — it had them all over its back! And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the spiked lizard!
kentrosaurus.superpower: Spikes all over its back AND its shoulders — a whole forest of spikes!
kentrosaurus.fait: Stegosaurus's African cousin! It had even more spikes — all the way to its shoulders! Even carnivores avoided attacking it from behind.
kentrosaurus.desc: Kentrosaurus was Stegosaurus's African cousin. It was smaller but had even more spikes all over its body. Even on its shoulders!

triceratops.name: Triceratops
triceratops.comp_hauteur: as tall as a basketball hoop!
triceratops.nom_etym: "Triceratops," three Greek pieces! Tri means three. Cerat means horn. And ops means what you see, the look, the face (the word comes from "eye"!). All together: the three-horned face!
triceratops.superpower: 3 horns and a giant bony frill — the perfect shield against T. rex!
triceratops.chasseurs: T. rex — but Triceratops fought back hard!
triceratops.amis: Maybe in herds, to protect the young
triceratops.fait: Its horns were 3 feet long! And scientists found T. rex bones with scars from Triceratops horns — they really did fight!
triceratops.desc: Triceratops had 3 horns and a big bony shield around its head. It wasn't afraid of T. rex! It was the great warrior of the plant-eaters.

torosaurus.name: Torosaurus
torosaurus.comp_taille: like two cars, one behind the other!
torosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a basketball hoop!
torosaurus.nom_etym: "Torosaurus," two Greek pieces! Toro, here, means punched through, holed — because of the big holes in its frill. (And no, it does NOT mean "bull"!) And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the holed-frill lizard!
torosaurus.superpower: One of the biggest heads of ANY animal that ever walked the Earth — its frill was almost 10 feet!
torosaurus.chasseurs: T. rex — same as its cousin Triceratops
torosaurus.amis: Maybe in small groups, like other horned dinos
torosaurus.fait: Its frill had big holes (like windows!), while Triceratops's frill was solid all the way through. That's how you tell them apart!
torosaurus.desc: Torosaurus looked a lot like Triceratops, but with an even bigger frill, punched through with two big holes. It had the biggest skull of any land animal!

protoceratops.name: Protoceratops
protoceratops.comp_hauteur: it would come up to your waist!
protoceratops.nom_etym: "Protoceratops," three Greek pieces! Proto means first — like a prototype! It's an early ancestor of the horned dinos. Cerat, horn. And ops, face, look. All together: the first horned face!
protoceratops.superpower: The grandfather of all the horned dinos! And a super powerful jaw.
protoceratops.amis: In herds, with nests grouped together
protoceratops.fait: Scientists found an incredible fossil: a Velociraptor and a Protoceratops that died mid-fight! Buried together by a sandstorm!
protoceratops.desc: Protoceratops was the little ancestor of Triceratops. It already had a frill, but no horns yet. And it fought bravely against Velociraptors!

pentaceratops.name: Pentaceratops
pentaceratops.comp_taille: as long as a road is wide — it takes up the whole street!
pentaceratops.comp_hauteur: as tall as a front door!
pentaceratops.nom_etym: "Pentaceratops," three Greek pieces! Penta means five — like a five-sided pentagon! Cerat, horn. And ops, face. All together: the five-horned face!
pentaceratops.superpower: One of the BIGGEST heads of any animal that ever walked the Earth — almost as big as Dad!
pentaceratops.fait: Its head (with the frill) measured over 7 feet — bigger than Dad standing up! One of the biggest heads in the whole animal kingdom.
pentaceratops.desc: Pentaceratops had "five horns": three real ones, plus two points on its cheeks. And a huge head, among the biggest of any land animal!

parasaurolophus.name: Parasaurolophus
parasaurolophus.comp_hauteur: as tall as two Dads standing on each other's shoulders!
parasaurolophus.nom_etym: "Parasaurolophus," three Greek pieces! Para means beside, almost the same as. Sauro, lizard. And lophus, crest. All together: almost the same as the "crested lizard" — with its big hollow horn for making music!
parasaurolophus.superpower: Its crest was a musical instrument! It blew air through it to make very loud sounds!
parasaurolophus.amis: In big herds — the calls warned the whole group of danger!
parasaurolophus.fait: Its hollow crest made sounds like a trombone! Scientists can even rebuild its music on a computer!
parasaurolophus.desc: Parasaurolophus had a big hollow crest on its head. It blew air through it to make very loud sounds — like a giant horn — to talk to its herd!

corythosaurus.name: Corythosaurus
corythosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a front door!
corythosaurus.nom_etym: "Corythosaurus," two Greek pieces! Corytho means helmet — its crest looked like a Greek warrior's helmet! And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the helmet lizard! And "casuarius"? That compares its crest to a cassowary, a big bird with a crest on its head, a bit like this dino!
corythosaurus.superpower: Its crest was hollow inside — it made its voice echo like a trumpet, to talk to its herd, even from far away!
corythosaurus.amis: In herds — the crest was used to warn others of danger!
corythosaurus.fait: Its helmet-shaped crest wasn't just for looks: inside, tiny bony tubes made its voice echo, like a hollow musical instrument!
corythosaurus.desc: Corythosaurus wore a real helmet on its head — a rounded, hollow crest, like a Greek warrior's or a cassowary's. It lived in herds and may have used it to call to the others, even without seeing them!

maiasaura.name: Maiasaura
maiasaura.comp_hauteur: as tall as a soccer goal!
maiasaura.nom_etym: "Maiasaura," two Greek pieces! Maia means good mother. And saura, lizard — in the feminine, because it's a mom! All together: the good mother lizard. It got that name because scientists found its nests full of eggs and babies!
maiasaura.superpower: She took care of her babies at the nest, and brought them food while they were too small to leave!
maiasaura.chasseurs: Daspletosaurus, a cousin of T. rex, hunted the young ones. Small hunters like Troodon sometimes came to steal eggs from poorly guarded nests.
maiasaura.amis: In a huge colony, hundreds of nests side by side
maiasaura.fait: The nests were spaced about 23 feet apart: just the length of a mom, so she could turn around without crushing her neighbor's nest!
maiasaura.desc: Maiasaura is THE discovery that changed everything: before her, nobody knew dinosaurs took care of their babies. Scientists found dozens of nests in the same spot, with eggs, babies, and moms — they nicknamed the place Egg Mountain.

saurolophus.name: Saurolophus
saurolophus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a basketball hoop!
saurolophus.comp_poids: as heavy as a hippo and a horse put together!
saurolophus.nom_etym: "Saurolophus," two Greek pieces! Sauro means lizard. And lophus, crest. All together: the crested lizard! Its crest isn't hollow like Parasaurolophus's — it's solid bone, straight, pointing backward.
saurolophus.superpower: Lived on BOTH sides of the planet at the same time — in Canada AND in Mongolia, connected back then by a land bridge!
saurolophus.chasseurs: Albertosaurus in America, Tarbosaurus in Asia
saurolophus.amis: In big herds, young and old together
saurolophus.fait: In Mongolia, scientists found over a hundred Saurolophus in the same spot, babies and adults — caught together by a sudden flood.
saurolophus.desc: Saurolophus wears a long spike of solid bone on its skull, pointing backward. Scientists think it was used to be seen and recognized in the herd — not to make music, like Parasaurolophus's hollow crest. It lived in both Canada and Mongolia, on opposite sides of the world!

edmontosaurus.name: Edmontosaurus
edmontosaurus.comp_taille: as long as a school bus!
edmontosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as two Dads standing on each other's shoulders!
edmontosaurus.nom_etym: "Edmontosaurus" is named after a place! Edmonto comes from Edmonton, a city in Canada where its bones were found. And saurus (or saur), in Greek, lizard. All together: the Edmonton lizard!
edmontosaurus.superpower: Hundreds of teeth for chewing — never short of a spare!
edmontosaurus.fait: It had up to 1,000 small teeth that kept getting replaced! When one fell out, a new one grew in.
edmontosaurus.desc: Edmontosaurus was a big duck-billed dino. It lived in giant herds and had hundreds of teeth for grinding up the toughest plants!

iguanodon.name: Iguanodon
iguanodon.comp_hauteur: as tall as a soccer goal!
iguanodon.nom_etym: "Iguanodon" mixes two languages! Iguano comes from iguana (a lizard) — a word that comes from the Caribbean. And odon, in Greek, is tooth — its teeth looked like an iguana's! All together: the iguana tooth!
iguanodon.superpower: A bony spike on its thumb — like a knife built into its hand!
iguanodon.fait: It's one of the FIRST dinosaurs ever discovered, back in 1820! At first, scientists thought the thumb spike was a horn on its nose!
iguanodon.desc: Iguanodon is a famous dino because it's one of the first ever found. It had a sharp spike on its thumb for defense. It walked on 4 legs but could rear up on 2!

pachycephalosaurus.name: Pachycephalosaurus
pachycephalosaurus.comp_taille: as long as a big SUV!
pachycephalosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a car — you'd have to look up!
pachycephalosaurus.nom_etym: "Pachycephalosaurus," three Greek pieces! Pachy means thick (like "pachyderm"!). Cephalo, head. And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the thick-headed lizard — its skull was as hard as a helmet!
pachycephalosaurus.superpower: A skull 10 inches thick! It fought by head-butting, like rams do!
pachycephalosaurus.fait: Its skull was 10 inches thick — almost as thick as your whole head! Scientists think it may have fought by head-butting, just like rams do today.
pachycephalosaurus.desc: Pachycephalosaurus had a super thick skull, like a motorcycle helmet made of bone! Males fought by head-butting each other, just like rams do today.

velociraptor.name: Velociraptor
velociraptor.comp_hauteur: it would come up to your waist!
velociraptor.nom_etym: "Velociraptor," two Latin pieces! Veloci means fast — like "velocity"! And raptor is a thief who snatches things fast. All together: the fast thief!
velociraptor.superpower: Super clever, super fast, with one big retractable sickle claw!
velociraptor.amis: Mostly alone — raptor packs are a movie myth!
velociraptor.fait: The real Velociraptor was about the size of a turkey! And it had FEATHERS! Nothing like the big scaly movie monsters!
velociraptor.desc: Velociraptor wasn't huge — about the size of a big dog. But it was covered in feathers and super, super clever! It probably hunted alone or in pairs, not in big packs like in the movies.
velociraptor.queue_note: Its stiff tail made up half its length: that's why it's small overall, but so long and thin!

deinonychus.name: Deinonychus
deinonychus.nom_etym: "Deinonychus," two Greek pieces! Deino means terrible, fearsome — it's the same root as the word "dinosaur"! And nychus, claw. All together: the terrible claw — it had a huge curved claw!
deinonychus.superpower: Its huge 5 inch claw was a deadly weapon for hooking prey!
deinonychus.amis: May have hunted in groups — scientists still debate it!
deinonychus.fait: In the movies, the big scary "raptors" actually look like Deinonychus, not the small Velociraptor!
deinonychus.desc: Deinonychus had one huge, razor-sharp claw on each foot and may have hunted in groups. Super fast and super smart! It's the real deal behind the big movie raptors.

utahraptor.name: Utahraptor
utahraptor.comp_taille: as long as a road is wide — it takes up the whole street!
utahraptor.comp_hauteur: as tall as a front door!
utahraptor.nom_etym: "Utahraptor" mixes a place and Latin! Utah is the American state where it was found. And raptor, in Latin, is thief. All together: the thief from Utah!
utahraptor.superpower: The biggest claw of any raptor — 9 inches! Like a giant kitchen knife!
utahraptor.chasseurs: Nothing in its time dared attack it
utahraptor.fait: Its claw was 9 inches long — as long as your whole hand! It's the biggest raptor that ever lived!
utahraptor.desc: Utahraptor was a GIANT among raptors! It had a huge claw, ran fast, and was very smart. The top predator of its time!

microraptor.name: Microraptor
microraptor.comp_taille: like a big cat stretched out!
microraptor.comp_hauteur: it would come up to your knees!
microraptor.nom_etym: "Microraptor" is half Greek, half Latin! Micro, in Greek, means tiny — like a microbe! And raptor, in Latin, thief. All together: the little thief!
microraptor.superpower: 4 wings! It glided between trees like a flying squirrel!
microraptor.fait: It had 4 wings — 2 on its arms AND 2 on its legs! It glided between trees like a mini airplane!
microraptor.desc: Microraptor was tiny, with 4 wings! It glided between trees in China to catch lizards and small fish. Amazing!

troodon.name: Troodon
troodon.nom_etym: "Troodon," two Greek pieces! Troo means to wound, to cut. And odon, tooth — its small teeth had sharp edges. All together: the wounding tooth!
troodon.superpower: The SMARTEST dinosaur! The biggest brain compared to its body size!
troodon.amis: In groups, maybe tending eggs together
troodon.fait: Some scientists think that if the dinosaurs hadn't gone extinct, Troodon might have become as smart as a human within a few million more years!
troodon.desc: Troodon was the smartest dinosaur of them all! It had big eyes for seeing at night, long clever hands, and a huge brain. The dinosaur professor!

gallimimus.name: Gallimimus
gallimimus.comp_taille: as long as a road is wide — it takes up the whole street!
gallimimus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a front door!
gallimimus.nom_etym: "Gallimimus" mixes Latin and Greek! Galli, in Latin, means rooster, chicken. And mimus comes from Greek and means "one who imitates" — like a mime! All together: the chicken imitator — it ran like a giant ostrich!
gallimimus.superpower: The FASTEST dino — up to 31 miles an hour, as fast as a car in the city!
gallimimus.fait: It ran at 31 miles an hour — as fast as a car in the city! Many predators couldn't catch it.
gallimimus.desc: Gallimimus was the speed champion! It looked like a giant ostrich and ran in big herds. So fast that even T. rex couldn't catch it!

oviraptor.name: Oviraptor
oviraptor.nom_etym: "Oviraptor," two Latin pieces! Ovi means egg — like "oval"! And raptor, thief. All together: the egg thief — but really, it was guarding its OWN eggs, like a good dad!
oviraptor.superpower: A colorful parrot-like crest AND a devoted dad — it sat on its own eggs!
oviraptor.amis: In pairs, to raise the babies
oviraptor.fait: Its name means "egg thief"... but that was a mistake! Scientists later discovered it was sitting on its OWN eggs, just like a bird!
oviraptor.desc: Oviraptor got unfairly blamed for stealing eggs — really it was sitting on its own, just like a bird! It had a pretty colorful crest and was an excellent dad!

pteranodon.name: Pteranodon
pteranodon.comp_taille: wings spread as wide as a car and a half!
pteranodon.comp_hauteur: as tall as Dad standing up!
pteranodon.nom_etym: "Pteranodon," three Greek pieces! Pter means wing — like "pterodactyl"! An means "without." And odon, tooth. All together: the wing without teeth — it flew with a big beak, no teeth at all!
pteranodon.superpower: Flew effortlessly, riding warm air currents — the king of the skies!
pteranodon.fait: Not a real dinosaur — a flying reptile! Its crest steered its flight like a rudder. It dove to catch fish.
pteranodon.desc: Pteranodon wasn't a dinosaur but a flying reptile! It had a huge wingspan and glided on the wind. It fished by diving into the sea, like a giant pelican!

quetzalcoatlus.name: Quetzalcoatlus
quetzalcoatlus.comp_taille: wings spread as wide as a city bus!
quetzalcoatlus.comp_hauteur: almost as tall as three Dads standing on each other's shoulders!
quetzalcoatlus.nom_etym: "Quetzalcoatlus" is named after a god! Quetzalcoatl is the great feathered serpent god of the Aztecs, a people from Mexico — a real god's name! All together: the dinosaur of the feathered serpent god — the biggest flying creature of all time!
quetzalcoatlus.superpower: One of the biggest flying animals of ALL TIME! As tall as a standing giraffe!
quetzalcoatlus.chasseurs: Nothing could catch it in the air
quetzalcoatlus.proies: Small animals, insects, and crustaceans (caught on the ground)
quetzalcoatlus.fait: Standing on the ground it stood 17 feet tall — as tall as a giraffe... and yet it could FLY! One of the biggest flying creatures that ever existed!
quetzalcoatlus.desc: Quetzalcoatlus was the biggest flying creature in the whole history of Earth! Standing up, it was as tall as a giraffe. It flew for thousands of miles.

hatzegopteryx.name: Hatzegopteryx
hatzegopteryx.comp_taille: wings spread as wide as six Dads lying head to toe!
hatzegopteryx.comp_hauteur: as tall as a basketball hoop!
hatzegopteryx.nom_etym: "Hatzegopteryx thambema" splits into three! Hatzego comes from Hațeg, a region of Romania, in Europe, where its bones were found. Pteryx, in Greek, means wing. And thambema, a Greek word, means monster! All together: the monster wing from Hațeg — scientists named it that because of its huge size and enormous head!
hatzegopteryx.regime: 🥩 Carnivore (hunted on the ground, on its island)
hatzegopteryx.superpower: A massive head — among the biggest of any flying reptile — and it hunted just as well on foot as in the sky!
hatzegopteryx.chasseurs: None: on its island, it was the biggest hunter of all
hatzegopteryx.proies: Small dwarf dinosaurs from its island — miniature cousins of the long-necked giants and the duck-billed dinos
hatzegopteryx.amis: A loner, the only giant hunter on its island
hatzegopteryx.fait: Its head alone was as long as Dad lying flat on the ground! It lived on an island in Europe, where many dinosaurs had shrunk down small — but it stayed enormous, walking well on all four legs to hunt on the ground.
hatzegopteryx.desc: Hatzegopteryx lived on a remote island in the middle of the sea, in Europe — nowhere near America like its cousins Pteranodon and Quetzalcoatlus! On that island, most dinosaurs had become tiny. But it stayed huge, with a short, sturdy neck and an enormous beak, and it walked just as well as it flew to catch its prey.

archaeopteryx.name: Archaeopteryx
archaeopteryx.comp_taille: like a big cat stretched out!
archaeopteryx.comp_hauteur: it would come up to your knees!
archaeopteryx.nom_etym: "Archaeopteryx," two Greek pieces! Archeo means ancient, very old — like "archaeology"! And pteryx, wing, feather. All together: the ancient wing — it's one of the very first birds!
archaeopteryx.superpower: The FIRST bird in the world! The missing link between dinosaurs and birds!
archaeopteryx.fait: It's the ANCESTOR OF ALL BIRDS! It had feathers AND teeth AND claws. The most precious fossil in the world!
archaeopteryx.desc: Archaeopteryx is one of the very first birds! It had feathers like a bird, but also teeth and claws like a dino. Today's birds are its cousins.

mosasaurus.name: Mosasaurus
mosasaurus.comp_taille: as long as a school bus and a half!
mosasaurus.nom_etym: "Mosasaurus" is named after a river! Mosa is the Meuse, a river in Europe where its bones were found. And saurus (or saur), in Greek, lizard. All together: the lizard from the Meuse — a real sea monster!
mosasaurus.superpower: The sea monster — absolute king of every ocean in the Cretaceous!
mosasaurus.chasseurs: None — it was at the very top
mosasaurus.fait: It even caught flying reptiles, like Pteranodon, right out of the sky! And it ate sharks for breakfast!
mosasaurus.desc: Mosasaurus was the monster of prehistoric seas! As long as two cars, it ruled over every ocean. It even ate sharks and flying reptiles like Pteranodon!

baryonyx.name: Baryonyx
baryonyx.comp_hauteur: as tall as a soccer goal!
baryonyx.comp_poids: as heavy as a small car and a cow put together!
baryonyx.nom_etym: "Baryonyx," two Greek pieces! Bary means heavy. And onyx, claw. All together: the heavy claw — it had a huge claw for catching fish!
baryonyx.superpower: A huge claw on its thumb — 12 inches! For spearing fish!
baryonyx.fait: Discovered by a plumber in England! Scientists found fish scales AND Iguanodon bones in its stomach!
baryonyx.desc: Baryonyx had a huge claw for catching fish, like a fishing bear! Discovered in England, scientists found fish in its stomach. A true giant fisherman!

therizinosaurus.name: Therizinosaurus
therizinosaurus.comp_hauteur: almost as tall as three Dads standing on each other's shoulders!
therizinosaurus.nom_etym: "Therizinosaurus," two Greek pieces! Therizino means to scythe, to cut grass — like a scythe! And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the scythe lizard — its claws were long and curved like scythes!
therizinosaurus.superpower: The LONGEST claws of any animal — 20 inches! But it ate only plants!
therizinosaurus.chasseurs: Tarbosaurus — but the claws grew right back!
therizinosaurus.fait: It had claws 20 inches long — almost as long as your whole arm, and the longest of any animal! And yet it peacefully ate leaves and plants!
therizinosaurus.desc: Therizinosaurus had the longest claws in the whole history of animals — 20 inches each! But despite those scary claws, it only ate plants and leaves!

dimetrodon.name: Dimetrodon
dimetrodon.epoque: Permian · 280 million years ago (before the dinos!)
dimetrodon.comp_hauteur: as tall as Dad standing up!
dimetrodon.nom_etym: "Dimetrodon," three Greek pieces! Di means two. Metro, measure, size — like a "meter"! And odon, tooth — it had teeth of two different sizes! All together: the two-sized teeth. (And careful: it's not actually a dinosaur, it lived before them!)
dimetrodon.superpower: A big sail to soak up the sun — a living thermometer!
dimetrodon.fait: Careful: Dimetrodon is NOT a dinosaur! It lived 50 million years BEFORE them and is actually closer to us (mammals) than to the dinos!
dimetrodon.desc: Dimetrodon isn't a dinosaur — it's an ancestor of mammals! It lived long before the dinos. Its big back sail helped it warm up in the sun.

edaphosaurus.name: Edaphosaurus
edaphosaurus.epoque: Permian · 280 million years ago (before the dinos!)
edaphosaurus.comp_taille: like three 4-year-olds lying end to end!
edaphosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a car — you'd have to look up!
edaphosaurus.nom_etym: "Edaphosaurus," two Greek pieces! Edaphos means pavement, flat stone ground. And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the pavement-toothed lizard — because it had dozens of tiny teeth packed side by side, like paving stones, for crushing plants!
edaphosaurus.superpower: A big back sail, almost like Dimetrodon's — but this one ate only plants!
edaphosaurus.chasseurs: Dimetrodon, which lived in the same area
edaphosaurus.fait: It has almost the same sail as Dimetrodon — but it's the total opposite: Dimetrodon ate meat, while this one only ate plants. The shape doesn't tell you everything!
edaphosaurus.desc: Edaphosaurus isn't a dinosaur — it lived long before them. It's a very ancient cousin of furry animals, so a little bit of us! It carried a sail on its back, and crushed plants with its dozens of tiny paving-stone teeth.

gorgonops.name: Gorgonops
gorgonops.epoque: Permian · 260 million years ago (before the dinos!)
gorgonops.comp_taille: like a tall Dad lying on the ground!
gorgonops.comp_hauteur: it would come up to your belly button!
gorgonops.nom_etym: "Gorgonops," two Greek pieces! Gorgon is a monster from ancient Greek stories, so terrifying that just looking at it was scary. And ops means face. All together: the terrifying face — scientists found its skull genuinely frightening!
gorgonops.superpower: Two long pointed teeth like sabers, as long as your hand!
gorgonops.chasseurs: None — it was the biggest hunter of its time
gorgonops.proies: The big plant-eaters from before the dinos
gorgonops.fait: It's not a dinosaur: it's a cousin even closer to us than Dimetrodon! Its legs already stood a bit straighter under its body, like a dog's, instead of splayed out to the sides like a lizard's.
gorgonops.desc: Gorgonops isn't a dinosaur — it's a distant ancestor of furry animals, so a little bit of us! With its two long saber teeth, it was the biggest hunter in South Africa, long before the first dinosaurs.

lystrosaurus.name: Lystrosaurus
lystrosaurus.epoque: Permian · 250 million years ago (before the dinos!)
lystrosaurus.region: South Africa, Antarctica, India, China, Russia, Mongolia
lystrosaurus.comp_taille: like a big cat stretched out!
lystrosaurus.comp_hauteur: it would come up to your knees!
lystrosaurus.nom_etym: "Lystrosaurus," two Greek pieces! Lystron means shovel. And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the shovel lizard — because of its wide, flat snout, which looked like a little shovel!
lystrosaurus.superpower: The great survivor: it lived through the biggest disaster in the whole history of Earth!
lystrosaurus.chasseurs: Almost nothing left right after the disaster — most had disappeared
lystrosaurus.proies: None, it snipped low plants with its beak
lystrosaurus.fait: After the biggest disaster in Earth's history, in some places, almost every four-legged animal you find is a Lystrosaurus — sometimes more than nine out of ten!
lystrosaurus.desc: Lystrosaurus isn't a dinosaur — it's a distant cousin of furry animals. Small, with a horny beak like a turtle's, it survived the worst disaster Earth has ever known. Its bones turn up in Africa, China, India, and even Antarctica: back then, all the land was joined into one single piece.

moschops.name: Moschops
moschops.epoque: Permian · 265 million years ago (before the dinos!)
moschops.comp_taille: like three 4-year-olds lying end to end!
moschops.nom_etym: "Moschops," two Greek pieces! Moschos means calf — a baby cow. And ops, face. All together: the calf face — scientists thought its big head looked like a calf's!
moschops.superpower: A skull as thick as a helmet: it could charge head-first without hurting itself!
moschops.chasseurs: The big hunters of the Permian, like Gorgonops
moschops.amis: Measured up against other Moschops with head-butting contests
moschops.fait: The top of its skull was 2 inches thick — almost as wide as your hand! Two Moschops could charge head to head, like mountain sheep do today, to show who was stronger.
moschops.desc: Moschops isn't a dinosaur — it's a very ancient cousin of furry animals. Big and stocky, with a skull as thick as a helmet, it head-butted its rivals instead of biting them.

elasmosaurus.name: Elasmosaurus
elasmosaurus.comp_taille: as long as a school bus!
elasmosaurus.nom_etym: "Elasmosaurus," two Greek pieces! Elasmo comes from elasmos, which means thin plate — because the bones in its neck were flat and thin, like discs! And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the thin-plated lizard!
elasmosaurus.superpower: The longest neck of ANY reptile: 72 vertebrae, 23 feet of neck!
elasmosaurus.chasseurs: Mosasaurus (the fearsome predator of the seas)
elasmosaurus.fait: In 1868, a scientist glued the head... onto the wrong end! He mixed up the tail and the neck. His rival told him: you put it on backward! The biggest blunder in the history of paleontology!
elasmosaurus.desc: Elasmosaurus wasn't a dinosaur — it was a giant marine reptile from the Cretaceous! Its neck measured 23 feet, half its body length. It couldn't lift its head out of the water like in the movies.

ophthalmosaurus.name: Ophthalmosaurus
ophthalmosaurus.comp_poids: as heavy as a small car!
ophthalmosaurus.nom_etym: "Ophthalmosaurus," two Greek pieces! Ophthalmo comes from ophthalmos, which means eye — like an ophthalmologist, the eye doctor! And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the giant-eyed lizard!
ophthalmosaurus.superpower: GIANT eyes, 9 inches wide — among the biggest eyes of any animal, for seeing in the dark depths!
ophthalmosaurus.proies: Squid, fish caught in the dark water
ophthalmosaurus.fait: It's an ichthyosaur — a marine reptile shaped like a dolphin! Its eyes were so huge they took up almost its whole head. And like dolphins, it gave birth to live babies in the water, never laying eggs on land!
ophthalmosaurus.desc: Ophthalmosaurus wasn't a dinosaur — it was an ichthyosaur, a marine reptile that looked like a dolphin. With its huge eyes, it could spot prey in the dark depths of the ocean.

liopleurodon.name: Liopleurodon
liopleurodon.comp_taille: like two cars, one behind the other!
liopleurodon.comp_hauteur: as tall as a car — you'd have to look up!
liopleurodon.nom_etym: "Liopleurodon," three Greek pieces! Leios means smooth — its teeth had smooth edges, no ridges! Pleura means side. And odon, tooth. All together: the smooth-sided tooth — a scientific name for some seriously terrifying teeth!
liopleurodon.superpower: An incredible sense of smell: its forward-facing nostrils sniffed out prey from far away!
liopleurodon.chasseurs: None — the number one hunter in its seas
liopleurodon.proies: Giant fish, ichthyosaurs, other marine reptiles
liopleurodon.fait: A TV show in 1999 said it was 82 feet long — like four cars end to end! Real scientists corrected that: 20 to 23 feet. Much smaller, but still just as fearsome!
liopleurodon.desc: Liopleurodon was a pliosaur — a marine reptile with a short neck and a huge jaw. It hunted in European seas during the Jurassic. Its amazing sense of smell let it sniff out prey from far away.

archelon.name: Archelon
archelon.nom_etym: "Archelon," two Greek pieces! Arche means chief, first, the greatest — like in "archaeology"! And chelon, turtle. All together: the chief turtle, turtle number one — the biggest turtle of all time!
archelon.superpower: The biggest turtle that ever lived — 15 feet long!
archelon.chasseurs: Tylosaurus (a big mosasaur) and prehistoric sharks
archelon.fait: Its shell wasn't hard like a turtle's today — it was tough, leathery skin, like thick leather! With its big flippers, it flew through the water, like the leatherback turtles of today.
archelon.desc: Archelon wasn't a dinosaur — it was the biggest sea turtle that ever existed! Its shell was soft, like leather, not hard. It swam through Cretaceous seas with its big flippers.

shonisaurus.name: Shonisaurus
shonisaurus.comp_taille: as long as a school bus!
shonisaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as a front door!
shonisaurus.nom_etym: "Shonisaurus," two pieces! Shoni comes from the Shoshone Mountains, in Nevada — that's where its bones were found, in the desert! And saurus (or saur), in Greek, lizard. All together: the lizard from the Shoshone Mountains!
shonisaurus.superpower: Looked like a giant dolphin — but lived 170 million years before real dolphins!
shonisaurus.chasseurs: Once grown, no known predator — it was one of the biggest animals in its ocean
shonisaurus.amis: In big groups (37 skeletons found together!)
shonisaurus.fait: In Nevada, in what is now a desert, scientists found 37 skeletons together! Dozens of Shonisaurus may have stranded there, like whales do today. And Nevada was under the sea back then!
shonisaurus.desc: Shonisaurus wasn't a dinosaur — it was a giant Triassic ichthyosaur, a marine reptile shaped like a giant dolphin. Its bones were found in the Nevada desert, which was once under the ocean.

patagotitan.name: Patagotitan
patagotitan.comp_taille: like two and a half school buses, one behind the other!
patagotitan.nom_etym: "Titanosaurus," two pieces! Titano comes from Titan, in Greek — the giant, the biggest of all! And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the giant lizard — the biggest animal that ever walked the Earth!
patagotitan.superpower: One of the BIGGEST animals that ever walked the Earth! Its heart alone was the size of a small car!
patagotitan.chasseurs: As an adult, almost nobody: no bite marks have ever been found on its bones. The young had to watch out for Patagonia's big carnivores.
patagotitan.proies: Eats leaves way up in the treetops
patagotitan.fait: Scientists found 7 skeletons together in Patagonia, in southern Argentina! Its bones were so huge it took special trucks and giant cranes to move them. Scientists still argue over who was bigger: this one, or its cousin Argentinosaurus!
patagotitan.desc: Patagotitan was the biggest animal that ever walked the Earth. Even Brachiosaurus looked small next to it! It lived in herds in Argentina, and its enormous size protected it from the big carnivores.

centrosaurus.name: Centrosaurus
centrosaurus.comp_taille: as long as a big SUV!
centrosaurus.comp_hauteur: as tall as Dad standing up!
centrosaurus.nom_etym: "Centrosaurus," two Greek pieces! Kentron means point, sharp spike. And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the spiked lizard — its whole frill was lined with little spikes!
centrosaurus.superpower: Lived in GIANT herds — scientists found the bones of THOUSANDS of Centrosaurus together in one spot!
centrosaurus.fait: Scientists found the bones of THOUSANDS of Centrosaurus, all together! They traveled in giant herds. When they huddled together, no hunter dared come close.
centrosaurus.desc: Centrosaurus had a beautiful curved horn on its nose, like a crescent, and a frill lined with spikes. It lived in Canada in huge herds: when Gorgosaurus came near, the whole herd would bunch together for safety.

ichthyosaurus.name: Ichthyosaurus
ichthyosaurus.comp_hauteur: it would come up to your waist!
ichthyosaurus.nom_etym: "Ichthyosaurus," two Greek pieces! Ichthyo comes from ikhthus, which means fish. And saurus (or saur), lizard. All together: the fish lizard — a reptile that looked like a fish!
ichthyosaurus.superpower: HUGE eyes, protected by rings of bone, for seeing in the dark depths!
ichthyosaurus.chasseurs: The big pliosaurs of its time, like Rhomaleosaurus
ichthyosaurus.fait: It looked like a dolphin, but it was a reptile! It gave birth to live babies in the water, not eggs — just like whales and dolphins. And its flippers were made of webbed fingers, like a giant hand!
ichthyosaurus.desc: Ichthyosaurus wasn't a dinosaur — it was a marine reptile that looked like a dolphin. Its streamlined body sliced through the water like a torpedo. Nature invented the dolphin shape long before real dolphins existed!

mammuthus.name: Woolly Mammoth
mammuthus.region: Europe, Asia, and North America (cold regions)
mammuthus.comp_taille: as long as a big SUV!
mammuthus.comp_hauteur: as tall as two Dads standing on each other's shoulders!
mammuthus.nom_etym: "Mammuthus" is commonly called the woolly mammoth. Woolly means covered in wool, in long fur — like a giant living sweater to keep out the cold! It was a furry cousin of the elephant, built to live in the snow.
mammuthus.superpower: Thick fur and a layer of fat for surviving the freezing cold, where nothing else could last!
mammuthus.chasseurs: Prehistoric humans, its only real hunters
mammuthus.proies: None: it ate grass and small plants
mammuthus.fait: Its two big curved tusks could be longer than Dad lying down — over 13 feet! It used them to sweep away snow and find the hidden grass underneath.
mammuthus.desc: The Woolly Mammoth lived during the Ice Age, when the Earth was cold and covered in snow. Covered in long fur with a big fatty hump, it crossed the frozen plains in herds. The very last ones died out just four thousand years ago.

smilodon.name: Smilodon
smilodon.comp_taille: like a tall Dad lying on the ground!
smilodon.nom_etym: "Smilodon," two Greek pieces! Smilo comes from smile, which means knife. And odon means tooth. All together: the knife tooth — because of its two huge pointed fangs, long like knives!
smilodon.superpower: Two fangs as long as your hand, for taking down prey with one precise strike!
smilodon.proies: Bison, wild horses, young giant sloths
smilodon.amis: May have lived in groups, like lions
smilodon.fait: People call it the saber-toothed tiger, but it wasn't a tiger! Its fangs measured almost 8 inches, longer than your hand. It could open its jaw much wider than a lion.
smilodon.desc: Smilodon was a great Ice Age hunter, stockier and more muscular than a lion. Its two giant teeth were its main weapon. Thousands of them were found trapped in a sticky tar pit in America, where they got stuck.

megatherium.name: Megatherium
megatherium.comp_taille: as long as a road is wide — it takes up the whole street!
megatherium.comp_hauteur: as tall as two Dads standing on each other's shoulders!
megatherium.nom_etym: "Megatherium," two Greek words! Mega means giant, huge. And therium comes from therion, which means beast, animal. All together: the giant beast — a good name, since it was a sloth as big as an elephant!
megatherium.superpower: Standing straight up on its back legs to reach leaves way up in the trees!
megatherium.chasseurs: Its huge size protected it; maybe Smilodon went after the young ones
megatherium.proies: None: it ate leaves and branches
megatherium.fait: It was a sloth, but a giant one! When it reared up on its back legs against a tree, it was taller than two Dads stacked up. Its front claws were as long as your forearm, for grabbing branches.
megatherium.desc: Megatherium was a giant ground sloth, as big as an elephant. Instead of climbing trees like small sloths do today, it stood up on the ground to eat leaves from the top. It lived peacefully in South America.

paraceratherium.name: Paraceratherium
paraceratherium.epoque: After the dinos · 30 million years ago
paraceratherium.comp_taille: like two cars, one behind the other!
paraceratherium.comp_hauteur: almost as tall as three Dads standing on each other's shoulders!
paraceratherium.nom_etym: "Paraceratherium" is a bit of a long word! Cerat, in Greek, means horn, and therium means beast. It was a giant cousin of the rhinoceros — except this one had NO horn at all!
paraceratherium.superpower: The biggest furry animal that ever walked the Earth — taller than a giraffe!
paraceratherium.chasseurs: Nobody: far too big to attack!
paraceratherium.proies: None: it ate leaves way up in the treetops
paraceratherium.fait: It was a cousin of the rhinoceros, but with NO horn, and absolutely giant: its head reached 16 feet up, taller than a giraffe! It's the biggest furry animal that ever existed.
paraceratherium.desc: Paraceratherium was a giant hornless rhinoceros, so big it towered over every other furry animal in history. With its long legs and long neck, it reached leaves way up in the trees, where nobody else could eat.

glyptodon.name: Glyptodon
glyptodon.comp_taille: like three 4-year-olds lying end to end!
glyptodon.comp_hauteur: as tall as a car — you'd have to look up!
glyptodon.comp_poids: as heavy as a small car!
glyptodon.nom_etym: "Glyptodon," two Greek words! Glypto comes from gluptos, which means carved, sculpted — because of the pretty patterns on its shell. And odon, tooth. All together: the sculpted tooth.
glyptodon.superpower: A huge, round, hard shell on its back, like a living shield — impossible to bite through!
glyptodon.chasseurs: Its shell protected it from almost everything
glyptodon.fait: It looked like a giant turtle, but it was a cousin of the armadillo! Its round shell was as big as a small car. And its cousin the Doedicurus even had a club at the end of its tail, like Ankylosaurus!
glyptodon.desc: Glyptodon was a big shelled animal, about the size of a small car. Its hard, rounded shell protected it like armor. It was a distant cousin of today's small armadillos, just a lot, lot bigger.

aenocyon.name: Dire Wolf
aenocyon.comp_taille: like a tall Dad lying on the ground!
aenocyon.nom_etym: "Aenocyon dirus," Greek and Latin! Cyon, in Greek, means dog. And dirus, in Latin, means terrible, fearsome. All together: the terrible dog — that's why it's called the dire wolf!
aenocyon.superpower: A stronger bite and a stockier body than today's wolf!
aenocyon.chasseurs: Smilodon, when they fought over a kill
aenocyon.fait: It looked like a wolf, but stockier, with a bigger head and stronger teeth. And surprise: scientists discovered it wasn't even a true wolf, just a distant cousin!
aenocyon.desc: The Dire Wolf hunted in packs during the Ice Age, like wolves do today, but it was heavier and more muscular. Thousands of them were found in the great tar pit in America, right alongside the Smilodons.

coelodonta.name: Woolly Rhino
coelodonta.comp_hauteur: as tall as a car — you'd have to look up!
coelodonta.comp_poids: as heavy as a small car and a cow put together!
coelodonta.nom_etym: "Coelodonta," two Greek words! Coelo means hollow, and odonta means teeth — because its teeth were a bit hollow inside. Most people just call it the woolly rhino: woolly, because it was covered in long fur to survive the cold.
coelodonta.superpower: A big horn on its nose, as long as your arm, for sweeping away snow and finding grass!
coelodonta.proies: None: it grazed on grass in the cold plains
coelodonta.fait: It was a rhino covered head to toe in fur! Its big front horn could be as long as your arm. It used it like a broom to push away the snow and eat the grass hidden underneath.
coelodonta.desc: The Woolly Rhino lived in the cold of the Ice Age, alongside the mammoths. Covered in thick fur, it carried two horns on its nose, one of them very long. Prehistoric humans even painted it on cave walls!

titanis.name: Titanis
titanis.epoque: After the dinos · 3 million years ago
titanis.comp_hauteur: as tall as a front door!
titanis.nom_etym: "Titanis" comes from the Titans, the all-powerful giants of old Greek stories. It got that name because it was a giant bird! It's also nicknamed the terror bird.
titanis.superpower: Running super fast on two big legs and striking with a huge hooked beak!
titanis.chasseurs: Few animals dared attack such a big hunter
titanis.fait: It was a bird, but far too big and heavy to fly: it ran instead! Standing up, it was as tall as a door. And its hooked beak, bigger than your head, was its main weapon.
titanis.desc: Titanis was a terror bird, a giant bird that couldn't fly. It ran on two big legs to hunt, with a huge pointed beak. It's the only terror bird that ever made it to North America, long after the dinosaurs.

pangee.soustitre: When all the continents were stuck together!
pangee.intro: Before the dinosaurs, all the continents on Earth were stuck together in one giant piece! We call it Pangea. You could walk from Africa all the way to America, no boat needed!
pangee.credit: Maps: C. Scotese / PALEOMAP — Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0

trias.label: Triassic
trias.texte: Back when the first dinosaurs lived, the whole world was one giant supercontinent: Pangea. It was hot and dry almost everywhere.

jurassique.label: Jurassic
jurassique.texte: Pangea slowly splits into two big pieces. A huge ocean opens up in the middle. Dinosaurs on each side can't see each other anymore!

cretace.label: Cretaceous
cretace.texte: The continents keep drifting apart, slowly, like giant rafts. It's starting to look like the Earth we know today!

present.label: Today
present.texte: After millions of years, the continents ended up right where they are today. And they're still moving… very, very slowly!

pangee.fun_fact: The continents are still moving today! But super slowly — about as fast as your fingernails grow!
pangee.pourquoi: That's why Cryolophosaurus lived in Antarctica: back then it was warm there, and it was stuck to the other lands!

meteorite.texte: A rock 6 miles wide comes crashing down from the sky into what is now Mexico. The explosion is 10 billion times more powerful than an atomic bomb. Everything burns for thousands of miles around. This is the most likely theory!

volcan.texte: In India, gigantic volcanoes spew out lava and gas for thousands of years. The smoke poisons the air and heats up the Earth. The Deccan volcanoes covered half of India in lava!

cendres.texte: After the meteorite hits, a cloud of dust and ash blocks out the sun for months… maybe even years! Without sun, the plants die. Without plants, the plant-eaters die. Without plant-eaters, the meat-eaters die.

froid.texte: The Earth plunges into darkness and cold. The temperature drops 18 to 36 degrees Fahrenheit everywhere on Earth. Tropical plants die. The oceans grow colder. It's a winter that lasts for years!

survivants.texte: The small animals that ate seeds and could hide away survive. Birds — which are real dinosaurs! — make it through. Crocodiles, turtles, and lizards hold on. Life starts over… and millions of years later, humans show up!

extinction.fun_fact: Birds are REAL dinosaurs! Every time you see a pigeon, you're looking at a dinosaur!

paleo.label: Paleozoic
paleo.accroche: Before the dinosaurs, life invents everything: fish, plants, first steps on land.

meso.label: Mesozoic
meso.accroche: The age of dinosaurs: three periods, from tiny to giant.

ceno.label: Cenozoic
ceno.accroche: After the dinosaurs, mammals grow bigger, all the way to you.
